subtitle: How Copper, Land and Law Forged the Vakataka Realm

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of a copperplate charter held in Pravarasena II’s hand, gleaming against a backdrop of fields and distant villages
panels.action: Pravarasena II stands in royal robes at the edge of a vast countryside, holding up a freshly engraved copperplate while villages, forests and rivers stretch behind him under a wide Deccan sky.

dialogue.text: In the age of Pravarasena II, the Vakataka king did not rule only with swords and forts, but with copperplates that turned land, taxes and memory into the very bones of his state.

i18n.hi: प्रवरसेन द्वितीय के समय में वाकाटक राजा सिर्फ़ तलवार और क़िले से नहीं, ताम्रपत्रों से राज करता है, जो ज़मीन, लगान और याद को उसके राज्य की हड्डियाँ बना देते हैं।

panels.shot: wide aerial over the Deccan plateau, early morning haze over rivers, forests and scattered settlements
panels.action: A sweeping view of Vidarbha and beyond shows clustered villages, winding rivers and patches of forest under soft morning light, with smoke rising from cooking fires.

dialogue.text: Fourth and fifth century. Across Vidarbha, Tripuri, Thalner and Balaghat, small villages dot the land. Behind their quiet fields, a new way of ruling is taking shape.

i18n.hi: चौथी–पाँचवीं सदी। विदर्भ, त्रिपुरी, थालनेर और बालाघाट में छोटे गाँव बिखरे हैं। शांत खेतों के पीछे राज करने का नया तरीक़ा जन्म ले रहा है।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a village household, focus on an oil lamp and a few worn coins on a mat
panels.action: Inside a modest village house, an oil lamp flickers beside a small heap of rare coins and measuring rods laid neatly on a woven mat.

dialogue.text: We know little of Vakataka coins. The metal is scarce in our record. Instead, their world speaks to us through copperplates that survived where market ledgers did not.

i18n.hi: वाकाटक सिक्कों के बारे में हमें थोड़ा ही पता है। धातु हमारे रिकॉर्ड में कम है। उनकी दुनिया हमसे बाज़ार के बही–खातों से नहीं, बचे हुए ताम्रपत्रों से बातें करती है।

panels.shot: tabletop close-up of stacked copperplates and seals, with a scribe’s hand entering frame
panels.action: On a low wooden desk lie stacked copperplates, their surfaces incised with fine lines, beside a royal seal and a reed stylus resting in an inkpot as a scribe’s hand reaches in.

dialogue.text: These plates, found at Poona, Riddhapur, Chammak, Thalner and Balaghat, are not simple gifts. They are charters, laying out villages, dues, officers and exemptions in hard, enduring metal.

i18n.hi: पूना, रिद्धापुर, चमक, थालनेर और बालाघाट की ये ताम्रपत्र सिर्फ़ दान नहीं हैं। ये फ़रमान हैं, जो गाँव, लगान, अफ़सर और छूटें कठोर, टिकाऊ धातु पर दर्ज करते हैं।

panels.shot: split wide shot: on one side Prabhavatigupta in court; on the other, fields and a village she grants
panels.action: On the left, a regal Prabhavatigupta sits in a palace hall with attendants; on the right, separated by a compositional divide, a rural village with fields and bullock carts thrives under the sun.

dialogue.text: Before Pravarasena II, his mother Prabhavatigupta, regent and Gupta princess, issues the Poona and Riddhapur plates, granting villages and rights as she holds the kingdom together.

i18n.hi: प्रवरसेन द्वितीय से पहले उसकी माँ, प्रभावतीगुप्ता — रीजेंट और गुप्त राजकुमारी — पूना और रिद्धापुर की पट्टियाँ निकालती है, गाँव और हक़ बाँटते हुए राज्य को थामे रहती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a copperplate engraving scene, focus on artisans working the plate
panels.action: Artisans sit cross-legged in a workshop, one hammering gently as another incises fine Nagari script onto a glowing copper sheet clamped on a low anvil.

dialogue.text: On each plate, the engraver cuts every line: the king’s lineage, the donee’s name, the village boundaries, the taxes remitted, the penalties for interference. Nothing is left to rumour.

i18n.hi: हर पट्टी पर क़लमगार हर बात उकेरता है: राजा की वंशावली, दान पाने वाले का नाम, गाँव की हदें, छोड़े गए कर, दखल देने की सज़ा। अफ़वाह के लिए कुछ नहीं छोड़ा जाता।

panels.shot: regal interior wide shot, Pravarasena II on the throne, advisors around, map spread before them
panels.action: Pravarasena II sits upright on a carved throne, advisors gathered around a painted cloth map on the floor that shows rivers and place-names, while a scribe kneels with a copperplate draft.

dialogue.text: When Pravarasena II rules, his Chammak, Thalner and Balaghat plates do more than pious donation. They map the realm itself, village by village, naming rivers, fields and neighbouring settlements.

i18n.hi: जब प्रवरसेन द्वितीय राज करता है, उसके चमक, थालनेर और बालाघाट के ताम्रपत्र महज़ धार्मिक दान से आगे बढ़ जाते हैं। वे राज्य का नक्शा बनाते हैं, गाँव–गाँव, नदियाँ, खेत और आस–पास की बसाहटें नाम से जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: closer three-quarter view of Pravarasena II gesturing to the scribe, scribe poised to write
panels.action: Pravarasena II leans forward, one hand resting on the map, the other raised in a calm directive toward a seated scribe who waits with stylus ready over a blank copper sheet.

dialogue.speaker: pravarasena_ii
dialogue.text: Write clearly: which fields, which houses, which dues are withdrawn, and for whom.

i18n.hi: साफ़ लिखो: कौन से खेत, कौन से घर, कौन सी लगान हटेगी, और किसके लिए।

panels.shot: tight close-up on engraved lines listing taxes and exemptions, with faint silhouettes of farmers in reflection
panels.action: The camera lingers on a section of the copperplate where tiny letters list specific exemptions from royal dues, the polished metal faintly reflecting imagined figures of farmers and officials.

dialogue.text: The plates spell out what is given up: land revenue, forced labour, fines, cesses. The crown renounces income in one place to bind new allies and religious networks in another.

i18n.hi: पट्टियाँ साफ़ बताती हैं क्या छोड़ा जा रहा है: ज़मीन का लगान, बेगारी, जुर्माने, सेस। ताज एक जगह कमाई छोड़ कर दूसरी जगह नए साथी और धार्मिक जाल बाँधता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Brahmin donee arriving at a grant village, villagers watching from doorways
panels.action: A learned Brahmin, staff and manuscripts in hand, walks into a village lane as men, women and children watch from doorways, some curious, some wary, bullocks tethered nearby.

dialogue.text: Many grants go to Brahmins and religious beneficiaries. In return, they offer ritual duties, learning, and a new node of loyalty that links distant hamlets to the king’s name.

i18n.hi: कई दान ब्राह्मणों और धार्मिक संस्थाओं को जाते हैं। बदले में वे पूजा, विद्या और वफ़ादारी का नया ठिकाना देते हैं, जो दूर–दूर के गाँवों को राजा के नाम से जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a local official reading out a copperplate to assembled villagers under a tree
panels.action: Under a broad tree, villagers sit in a semicircle as a local official holds up a copperplate and reads from it, his lips mid-utterance while faces show concern and curiosity.

dialogue.text: The charter is read aloud at the boundary. Names of officers, villagers and neighbours fix who must obey, who may collect, who is forbidden to interfere, on pain of curse and fine.

i18n.hi: फ़रमान सीमा पर ज़ोर से पढ़ा जाता है। अफ़सरों, गाँववालों और पड़ोसियों के नाम तय करते हैं किसे मानना है, कौन वसूल सकता है, किसे दखल से मना है — श्राप और जुर्माने के डर से।

panels.shot: documentary-style montage shot, faint overlays of RS Sharma and BD Chattopadhyaya as abstract scholars over a map and plates
panels.action: A thoughtful montage shows a modern map of central India, Vakataka copperplates laid over it, and ghostlike silhouettes of scholars studying them by lamplight, their faces turned to the plates.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, scholars argue. R.S. Sharma sees ‘Indian feudalism’ in these grants. B.D. Chattopadhyaya sees a more varied path of regional state formation, with many centres, many bargains.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद विद्वान बहस करते हैं। आर.एस. शर्मा इन दान में ‘भारतीय सामंतवाद’ देखते हैं। बी.डी. चट्टोपाध्याय कई केन्द्रों, कई सौदों वाली क्षेत्रीय राज्य–निर्माण की अलग राह देखते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a plate’s opening genealogy and royal eulogy, ornate but precise
panels.action: The engraved preamble of a copperplate fills the frame, with ornate lines praising the king’s ancestry and virtues, yet cut in an orderly, neat script.

dialogue.text: Each charter begins with praise and genealogy, but soon turns to measures and margins. Glory stands beside acreage, descent beside demarcation. Power is wrapped in poetry, executed in detail.

i18n.hi: हर फ़रमान स्तुति और वंश से शुरू होता है, पर जल्दी ही नाप–तौल और हदों पर उतर आता है। यश के साथ बीघा, वंश के साथ सरहद खड़ी होती है। ताक़त कविता में लिपटी है, पर काम बारीकी से होता है।

panels.shot: low-angle hero wide, Pravarasena II overseeing distribution of plates to couriers
panels.action: In a courtyard filled with mounted messengers, Pravarasena II stands tall as couriers kneel to receive sealed copperplates, tucking them into cloth bags before mounting their horses.

dialogue.text: From the royal centre, plates travel out with couriers. Each one shifts the flow of grain, labour and respect, moving a share of village life from king to donee, from court to countryside.

i18n.hi: राज–केन्द्र से पट्टियाँ दूतों के साथ बाहर निकलती हैं। हर एक अनाज, मेहनत और मान–सम्मान का बहाव मोड़ देती है, गाँव की ज़िंदगी का हिस्सा राजा से दानी तक, दरबार से देहात तक खिसक जाता है।

panels.shot: wide environmental shot of a grant village years later, with a small temple or matha established
panels.action: Years later, the same village shows a modest temple or matha by the fields, students and priests moving in and out as farmers plough nearby under the watch of a local functionary.

dialogue.text: Over time, some grant villages grow temples and mathas, new centres of learning and ritual. Others remain small, their exemption a quiet shift in who commands and who obeys in daily life.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ कई दान–गाँवों में मंदिर और मठ उठते हैं, विद्या और पूजा के नए केन्द्र बनते हैं। कुछ छोटे ही रहते हैं, उनकी छूट बस यही बदलती है कि रोज़मर्रा में कौन हुक्म देता है और कौन मानता है।

panels.shot: melancholic interior shot of a damaged plate half-buried in soil, unearthed by a modern digger’s hand
panels.action: A corroded copperplate lies half-buried in earth, a modern archaeologist’s hand brushing away soil as faint letters re-emerge from the patina in the soft light.

dialogue.text: When states crumble, their palaces vanish first. But these plates endure in the ground, waiting for chance spades and careful eyes to pull their cold, administrative prose back into the light.

i18n.hi: जब राज्य ढहते हैं, उनके महल सबसे पहले मिटते हैं। पर ये ताम्रपत्र ज़मीन में टिके रहते हैं, अचानक फावड़ों और चौकस आँखों का इंतज़ार करते हुए, ताकि उनकी ठंडी, दफ़्तर वाली गद्य फिर रोशनी में आ सके।

panels.shot: introspective medium close-up of Pravarasena II, eyes on a plate, background fading into darkness
panels.action: Pravarasena II sits alone, holding a copperplate on his lap, his face lit by lamplight while the background fades into shadow, giving a sense of quiet contemplation.

dialogue.speaker: pravarasena_ii
dialogue.text: When I am gone, these plates will still speak. But what will they say of me?

i18n.hi: जब मैं नहीं रहूँगा, ये पट्टियाँ फिर भी बोलेंगी। पर ये मेरे बारे में क्या कहेंगी?

panels.shot: final wide shot blending past and present: ghostly outlines of Vakataka officers over a modern landscape of villages
panels.action: A contemporary landscape of villages and fields in central India fills the frame, over which faint, transparent figures of ancient scribes, officers and kings stand aligned with old routes and rivers.

dialogue.text: Today, the Vakataka copperplates remind us that rule is not only battles and crowns. It is the patient writing of land, labour and law into records that outlive rulers and make power legible across time.

i18n.hi: आज वाकाटक ताम्रपत्र याद दिलाते हैं कि राज सिर्फ़ युद्ध और मुकुट नहीं है। यह भूमि, मेहनत और क़ानून को धैर्य से लिखना है, ऐसे रिकॉर्ड में जो राजाओं से ज़्यादा जीते हैं और ताक़त को समय के पार पढ़ने लायक बनाते हैं।

title_i18n.en: The Copperplate State of the Vakatakas

subtitle_i18n.en: How Copper, Land and Law Forged the Vakataka Realm
subtitle_i18n.hi: तांबा, ज़मीन और क़ानून से गढ़ा वाकाटक साम्राज्य
